addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

content.content:
1	# RISC-V Kernel Optimization Roadmap (Bonsai-4B Q1_0 / Ternary Q2_0)
2	
3	Primary model: models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf (572 MB, arch qwen3, 36 layers,
4	embd 2560, GQA with 1024-wide K/V projections, 253 MUL_MAT nodes per token
5	= 36 x 7 + lm_head).
6	
7	Why 4B (decision 2026-07-21, replaces the old 27B focus):
8	- Fits andesim hybrid's hard 2 GiB guest-RAM cap with room for KV cache and
9	  compute buffers (27B needs ~4.5 GB - blocked until andesim grows >2 GiB
10	  DRAM support).
11	- Plain qwen3: output is coherent on rv64. The qwen35 hybrid-attention bug
12	  (old F0) only affects 27B, so it no longer blocks anything - parked below.
13	- The full closed loop already works on 4B: end-to-end cycle-accurate
14	  per-kernel measurement under andesim hybrid marker mode was confirmed
15	  2026-07-16 (see Measurement setup).
16	
17	Hardware targets (both vsim engines, VLEN 512-2048 family per F4 design):
18	- vsim:ax45mpv_premium - VLEN=512, DLEN=512, ELEN=32, no zfh/zvfh.
19	- vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 - VLEN=1024, ELEN=64, first engine with real L3.
20	
21	Baselines:
22	- QEMU proxy (insn-count, -t 8, build-rv64-noomp, 2026-07-15):
23	  4B ~19-21 s/token. QEMU time tracks instruction count, not latency.
24	- Real cycles, hybrid marker ROI at K=51 (layer 7 V projection, 2560x1024,
25	  the smallest matmul in the model - nothing smaller exists per-layer):
26	  - ax45mpv_premium: 6528953 cycles (2026-07-16, stable across runs)
27	  - ax46mpv_fpga_l3: 4476168 cycles (2026-07-16, pristine upstream ggml)
28	  These are THE per-kernel before/after gate for F1-F7: same K, same model,
29	  real pipeline + memory system.
30	
31	Rules for every feature below:
32	- TDD: first add a correctness test comparing the new kernel against the
33	  matching *_generic function on random data (test-quantize-fns style),
34	  see it fail/pass, then optimize. Never commit a kernel without the test.
35	- Benchmark gate: QEMU proxy for correctness + rough insn counts, then
36	  hybrid marker ROI cycles before/after (the real number). FPGA only for
37	  final full-token figures.
38	
39	ELEN=32 constraint (ax45mpv_premium): no 64-bit vector elements anywhere.
40	Stock repack.cpp uses __riscv_vsseg4e64 -> GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF today; any
41	new F4 kernel must stay e32-clean (the Nx1 design already is: vlm masks,
42	int16 sumi, fp32 accumulators). Also: premium's FP datapath rejects LMUL=8
43	float ops (integer LMUL=8 is fine) - F4's VLEN=512 -> m4 fp32 mapping is
44	exactly at the safe limit; never use m8 for float.
45	
46	Status legend: TODO / IN-PROGRESS / DONE / PARKED
47	
48	---
49	
50	## F1. Q1_0 multi-row vec_dot (nrows = 2)
51	
52	- Status: TODO
53	- Description: The Q1_0 dot kernel recomputes/reloads the same activations
54	  for every weight row. Set `.nrows = 2` (later 4) so one call computes 2
55	  output elements: load + negate activations once, per row only do mask
56	  load (vlm) + vmerge + reduce. Expected ~1.5-2x on the dominant matmul path.
57	- Gate: K=51 ROI cycles before/after (V projection is exactly this path).
58	- Key files:
59	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484-578 (vl256/vl128 kernels + dispatcher)
60	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:227-232 (.nrows field of GGML_TYPE_Q1_0)
61	- Dependencies: none. Small diff, big win - good first step if F4 stalls.
62	
63	## F2. Q1_0 defer reductions - REMOVED
64	
65	- Status: REMOVED (2026-07-22, user decision). The vl512/vl512w candidate
66	  kernels were deleted from kernel-lab/ (q1_0.c/h, test harness); the lab
67	  dispatcher routes VLEN >= 256 to vl256 again. Rationale: it removed the
68	  per-group scalar stall but kept the horizontal reduction and the 32-lane
69	  fill, so it could never be more than a modest win; F4 (row-parallel
70	  repack) solves the actual problem and makes this path dead weight.
71	  Lesson kept for the record: QEMU TCG charges per vector instruction and
72	  makes scalar ops ~free, so this kind of stall-removal restructure READS
73	  AS A REGRESSION under QEMU (n=8192: vl256 57.5us vs vl512 75.5us) -
74	  never judge restructures by QEMU; only vsim/FPGA cycles count.
75	
76	## F3. Q1_0 full-VLEN utilization - FOLDED INTO F1/F4
77	
78	- Status: folded (2026-07-16 finding) - because Q8_0 activations are NOT
79	  contiguous (34-byte block stride), filling a 512-bit register costs slide
80	  instructions that cancel the saved vlm/vneg/vmerge. Wider vl alone cannot
81	  win for the vec_dot shape; width pays off only via repack (F4, contiguous
82	  interleaved rows) or multi-row amortization (F1). Not a standalone feature.
83	
84	## F4. Q1_0 repack, ROW-PARALLEL Nx1 (the wide-VLEN win)
85	
86	- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-22) - F4a DONE, F4b lab-verified pending
87	  cycle gate; largest expected win; supersedes F1-F3 for matmul.
88	- Core decision (2026-07-20, wide-VLEN analysis): use the ROW-PARALLEL
89	  `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like `ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic`,
90	  repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8` mmla-fold layout. Reason:
91	  * The 8x8 path uses vwmul/vwmacc + a vnsrl reduction tree (repack.cpp
92	    arch/riscv:161-177) - the multiplies exist to dequant 4-bit weights,
93	    and the fold tree is a horizontal reduction that under-uses wide VLEN
94	    (8 fp32 lanes, so 8/64 = 12% of a VLEN=2048 datapath). F3 already
95	    proved horizontal reductions are the bottleneck; the fold tree is one.
96	  * Q1_0 weights are +-1: the multiply collapses to a conditional add, and
97	    the ONLY reason to reduce (per-32 Q8_0 scale) is handled at group
98	    boundaries. Row-parallel keeps N rows in N lanes; the K-reduction
99	    becomes a loop-carried VERTICAL add per lane -> ZERO horizontal
100	    reductions in the whole kernel. This is the fix for VLEN 512-2048:
101	    spend LMUL on rows (useful work), not on one row's reduction.
102	- Layout `block_q1_0_Nx1` (N rows interleaved, per 128-col block, 18N bytes
103	  = N * sizeof(block_q1_0), same total size):
104	  * sign planes, column-major: for global col c in 0..127, N bits (one per
105	    row) -> 16N bytes, loadable as a per-column N-bit mask (vlm).
106	  * N fp16 weight scales (one d per row per 128-block) -> 2N bytes.
107	- RVV gemv inner loop (per 128-block, N rows in lanes, no reductions):
108	  ```
109	  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
110	  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128
111	      dy = fp16_to_fp32(a[g].d)                      // scalar (shared/rows)
112	      sumi[N] = 0                                    // int16, 32*127<32767 ok
113	      for c in 0..31:
114	          y    = a[g].qs[c]                          // scalar int8
115	          mask = vlm(sign plane col 32*g+c)          // N bits
116	          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes

119	  sumf[N] = vfmacc_vv(sumf, dx[N], facc_block)       // vector weight scale
120	  // after K loop: store sumf[N] to N contiguous outputs
121	  ```

# RISC-V Kernel Optimization Roadmap (Bonsai-4B Q1_0 / Ternary Q2_0)

Primary model: models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf (572 MB, arch qwen3, 36 layers,
embd 2560, GQA with 1024-wide K/V projections, 253 MUL_MAT nodes per token
= 36 x 7 + lm_head).

Why 4B (decision 2026-07-21, replaces the old 27B focus):
- Fits andesim hybrid's hard 2 GiB guest-RAM cap with room for KV cache and
  compute buffers (27B needs ~4.5 GB - blocked until andesim grows >2 GiB
  DRAM support).
- Plain qwen3: output is coherent on rv64. The qwen35 hybrid-attention bug
  (old F0) only affects 27B, so it no longer blocks anything - parked below.
- The full closed loop already works on 4B: end-to-end cycle-accurate
  per-kernel measurement under andesim hybrid marker mode was confirmed
  2026-07-16 (see Measurement setup).

Hardware targets (both vsim engines, VLEN 512-2048 family per F4 design):
- vsim:ax45mpv_premium - VLEN=512, DLEN=512, ELEN=32, no zfh/zvfh.
- vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 - VLEN=1024, ELEN=64, first engine with real L3.

Baselines:
- QEMU proxy (insn-count, -t 8, build-rv64-noomp, 2026-07-15):
  4B ~19-21 s/token. QEMU time tracks instruction count, not latency.
- Real cycles, hybrid marker ROI at K=51 (layer 7 V projection, 2560x1024,
  the smallest matmul in the model - nothing smaller exists per-layer):
  - ax45mpv_premium: 6528953 cycles (2026-07-16, stable across runs)
  - ax46mpv_fpga_l3: 4476168 cycles (2026-07-16, pristine upstream ggml)
  These are THE per-kernel before/after gate for F1-F7: same K, same model,
  real pipeline + memory system.

Rules for every feature below:
- TDD: first add a correctness test comparing the new kernel against the
  matching *_generic function on random data (test-quantize-fns style),
  see it fail/pass, then optimize. Never commit a kernel without the test.
- Benchmark gate: QEMU proxy for correctness + rough insn counts, then
  hybrid marker ROI cycles before/after (the real number). FPGA only for
  final full-token figures.

ELEN=32 constraint (ax45mpv_premium): no 64-bit vector elements anywhere.
Stock repack.cpp uses __riscv_vsseg4e64 -> GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF today; any
new F4 kernel must stay e32-clean (the Nx1 design already is: vlm masks,
int16 sumi, fp32 accumulators). Also: premium's FP datapath rejects LMUL=8
float ops (integer LMUL=8 is fine) - F4's VLEN=512 -> m4 fp32 mapping is
exactly at the safe limit; never use m8 for float.

Status legend: TODO / IN-PROGRESS / DONE / PARKED

---

## F1. Q1_0 multi-row vec_dot (nrows = 2)

- Status: TODO
- Description: The Q1_0 dot kernel recomputes/reloads the same activations
  for every weight row. Set `.nrows = 2` (later 4) so one call computes 2
  output elements: load + negate activations once, per row only do mask
  load (vlm) + vmerge + reduce. Expected ~1.5-2x on the dominant matmul path.
- Gate: K=51 ROI cycles before/after (V projection is exactly this path).
- Key files:
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484-578 (vl256/vl128 kernels + dispatcher)
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:227-232 (.nrows field of GGML_TYPE_Q1_0)
- Dependencies: none. Small diff, big win - good first step if F4 stalls.

## F2. Q1_0 defer reductions - REMOVED

- Status: REMOVED (2026-07-22, user decision). The vl512/vl512w candidate
  kernels were deleted from kernel-lab/ (q1_0.c/h, test harness); the lab
  dispatcher routes VLEN >= 256 to vl256 again. Rationale: it removed the
  per-group scalar stall but kept the horizontal reduction and the 32-lane
  fill, so it could never be more than a modest win; F4 (row-parallel
  repack) solves the actual problem and makes this path dead weight.
  Lesson kept for the record: QEMU TCG charges per vector instruction and
  makes scalar ops ~free, so this kind of stall-removal restructure READS
  AS A REGRESSION under QEMU (n=8192: vl256 57.5us vs vl512 75.5us) -
  never judge restructures by QEMU; only vsim/FPGA cycles count.

## F3. Q1_0 full-VLEN utilization - FOLDED INTO F1/F4

- Status: folded (2026-07-16 finding) - because Q8_0 activations are NOT
  contiguous (34-byte block stride), filling a 512-bit register costs slide
  instructions that cancel the saved vlm/vneg/vmerge. Wider vl alone cannot
  win for the vec_dot shape; width pays off only via repack (F4, contiguous
  interleaved rows) or multi-row amortization (F1). Not a standalone feature.

## F4. Q1_0 repack, ROW-PARALLEL Nx1 (the wide-VLEN win)

- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-22) - F4a DONE, F4b lab-verified pending
  cycle gate; largest expected win; supersedes F1-F3 for matmul.
- Core decision (2026-07-20, wide-VLEN analysis): use the ROW-PARALLEL
  `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like `ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic`,
  repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8` mmla-fold layout. Reason:
  * The 8x8 path uses vwmul/vwmacc + a vnsrl reduction tree (repack.cpp
    arch/riscv:161-177) - the multiplies exist to dequant 4-bit weights,
    and the fold tree is a horizontal reduction that under-uses wide VLEN
    (8 fp32 lanes, so 8/64 = 12% of a VLEN=2048 datapath). F3 already
    proved horizontal reductions are the bottleneck; the fold tree is one.
  * Q1_0 weights are +-1: the multiply collapses to a conditional add, and
    the ONLY reason to reduce (per-32 Q8_0 scale) is handled at group
    boundaries. Row-parallel keeps N rows in N lanes; the K-reduction
    becomes a loop-carried VERTICAL add per lane -> ZERO horizontal
    reductions in the whole kernel. This is the fix for VLEN 512-2048:
    spend LMUL on rows (useful work), not on one row's reduction.
- Layout `block_q1_0_Nx1` (N rows interleaved, per 128-col block, 18N bytes
  = N * sizeof(block_q1_0), same total size):
  * sign planes, column-major: for global col c in 0..127, N bits (one per
    row) -> 16N bytes, loadable as a per-column N-bit mask (vlm).
  * N fp16 weight scales (one d per row per 128-block) -> 2N bytes.
- RVV gemv inner loop (per 128-block, N rows in lanes, no reductions):
  ```
  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128
      dy = fp16_to_fp32(a[g].d)                      // scalar (shared/rows)
      sumi[N] = 0                                    // int16, 32*127<32767 ok
      for c in 0..31:
          y    = a[g].qs[c]                          // scalar int8
          mask = vlm(sign plane col 32*g+c)          // N bits
          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes
          sumi = vadd_vx_m(mask, sumi, 2*y)          // +2y where bit set => +-y
      facc_block = vfmacc_vf(facc_block, dy, vfcvt(sumi))   // scalar dy
  sumf[N] = vfmacc_vv(sumf, dx[N], facc_block)       // vector weight scale
  // after K loop: store sumf[N] to N contiguous outputs
  ```
  ~3 ops/col (1 vlm + vsub_vx + vadd_vx_m), all N-wide; ~393 N-wide ops per
  block-tile => ~6 ops/row/block at N=64 vs ~20 for single-row vec_dot, AND
  full VLMAX, AND no reduction stalls. Per-column vlm (128/block) is the
  main tuning point. Everything is e8/e16/e32 - ELEN=32-clean by design.
- N and LMUL mapping: fix N=64, adapt LMUL to vlenb at runtime so the fp32
  accumulator is full: VLEN=2048->m1, 1024->m2 (fpga_l3), 512->m4 (premium,
  FP-LMUL limit respected). One repacked type; nc must be a multiple of
  N=64 (2560 and 1024 both are; machinery handles remainder).
- Sub-features (do in order):
  * F4a - DONE (2026-07-22, kernel-lab): `repack_q1_0_to_q1_0_64x1` +
    `gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0_generic` (keeps the reference float-op order) +
    test_repack_gemv: bit-exact vs per-row vec_dot_generic on the original
    data, shapes up to nr=192/n=1024, random + 0x00/0xFF edges. TDD:
    zero-stub RED first, then GREEN.
  * F4b - lab kernels DONE, cycle gate PENDING (2026-07-22): vl512
    (i16m2/f32m4, premium FP-LMUL max) + vl1024 (i16m1/f32m2) + vlenb
    dispatcher in kernel-lab/q1_0.c. Scale expand via integer bit math
    (lab_expand_fp16_64_*) - no zfh/zvfh needed, premium-safe. Correctness:
    double-ref gate PASS at VLEN 512/1024 (max_norm_err 2.7e-06), generic
    path at 256/128. Generated asm clean: 3-insn column loop (vlm + vsub.vx
    + masked vadd.vx), no spills. QEMU --bench proxy on K=51 shape
    (2560x1024): 0.73x vs per-row vec_dot - EXPECTED artifact (TCG helper
    cost on masked ops/vlm; same lesson as removed F2, do NOT tune to it).
    MEASURED on RTL (2026-07-23, standalone rdcycle shootout at
    vsim-demo/q1_0, nr=64 x n=512, warm, results match on both):
      fpga_l3      VLEN=1024:  vl256  829 cyc/row -> gemv 125 cyc/row = 6.6x
      premium_full VLEN=512 :  vl256 1044 cyc/row -> gemv 174 cyc/row = 6.0x
      (M=1 premium_full-era record; the CANONICAL M=4 table with the new
      engines premium_max + HVM placement is in F4c below)
    Extrapolated K=51 (2560x1024, 8 blocks/row): fpga_l3 4.2M -> ~0.64M,
    premium ~5.3M -> ~0.9M; ~5-6x on the matmul portion of the ROI.
    Engine note: plain sim_ax45mpv_premium is built from a NDS_FELEN=0
    config (NO vector FP - every vf* traps); the VLEN=512+FP engine is
    sim_ax45mpv_premium_full (added to vsim_andesim config.yaml 2026-07-23,
    premium RTL + data/configs/ax45mpv_premium_full.cfg, FELEN=32 = fp32
    vector only, enough for zve32f). Its probe passes ALL vector-FP ops
    including vfwcvt.f.x.v - the vsext+vfcvt split in the kernel is
    optional there (kept: portable, ~free).
    Engine specs (from the cfg files):
      sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3     : VLEN/DLEN 1024, FELEN 64, L1 32K/32K,
                                L2 DISABLED (0), L3 2MB enabled
      sim_ax45mpv_premium_full: VLEN/DLEN 512, FELEN 32, L1 64K I$/8K D$,
                                L2 32KB enabled, no L3; ILM 1MB/DLM 32KB
    The 8KB D$ on premium (< lab warm set ~15KB) means its warm reps lean
    on L2; fpga_l3 warm reps are L1-resident.
    Remaining gate: K=51 marker ROI after F4d wiring.
  * F4c - gemm (M>1 prefill) - lab kernel DONE + MEASURED (2026-07-23,
    vsim-demo/q1_0 `q1_0_gemm_64x1`, nr=64 x n=512 x M=4, TDD RED->GREEN,
    QEMU ALL PASS at 512/1024, then RTL rdcycle, warm rep, ALL PASS):
      CANONICAL (engines = fpga_l3 + premium_max, cyc/dot warm):
        fpga_l3     1024 tile4: RAM 840/126/40  | HVM 785/92/37
        premium_max  512 tile2: RAM 1045/135/75 | HVM 753/83/54
        (columns = vl256 baseline / gemv x4 / gemm)
      Best chain RAM-baseline -> HVM-gemm: fpga_l3 22.7x, premium_max 19.4x.
      History premium_full (8K D$): RAM 1049/206/109 - D$ was its bottleneck.
    Design: every sign-mask vlm (+ its addressing) is loaded once and shared
    by the whole M-tile; per extra activation only 2 int vector ops + 1
    scalar load. M-tile is register-budgeted: 4 at VLEN=1024
    (sumi m1 x4 + facc/sumf m2 x8 + dx/temp ~ 25 regs), only 2 at VLEN=512
    (f32m4 accumulators, ~29 regs); both compile with ZERO vector spills.
    Amortization tracks tile size: masks shared 4-way -> 3.1x, 2-way -> 1.9x.
    ggml wiring (ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0 interleave + mmid tile loop) is part
    of F4d. Dep: F4b (done).
    HVM A/B (2026-07-23, -DQ1_HVM=1, hvm.h CSR-probe allocator ported
    printf-free from ace-tq1, ALL data in HVM, numbers in canonical table):
      findings - D$ size only helps repack kernels (8K->32K: gemv 206->135)
      and never the vl256 baseline (latency-bound, not capacity-bound);
      HVM ignores D$ size entirely (premium_full HVM == premium_max HVM)
      and still beats 32K D$ on the vlm stream (83 vs 135); HVM reps are
      deterministic (rep0==rep1). K=51 fit: premium 256KB HVM holds a
      64-row strip (~22KB); fpga_l3 8MB holds the whole 2560x1024 repacked
      weight (360KB) -- room for ~22 such weights (in-model: 22 attn_v land
      in HVM, the rest overflow back to RAM).
    premium_max engine (2026-07-23): premium RTL re-elaborated with ELEN=64
      FELEN=64 PACKED_FP16=yes D$ 8K->32K (ax45mpv_premium_max.cfg) -
      builds, probe_max (rv64gcv) 15/15 ok incl. e64 + f64 + zvfh-encoded
      f16->f32. Premium was never hard-limited to ELEN32; config knobs.
  * F4d - ggml wiring DONE (2026-07-23, TDD RED->GREEN), K=51 gate PENDING:
    block_q1_0x64 + repack_q1_0_to_q1_0_64_bl + generic gemv/gemm (bit-exact
    vs vec_dot order) in repack.cpp; RVV kernels (runtime vlenb dispatch:
    m1/m2 @VLEN>=1024 tile4, m2/m4 @512 tile2, vlm +-y hot loop, integer
    fp16 expand, vsext+vfcvt) in arch/riscv/repack.cpp; traits instance +
    dispatch (Q1_0 + riscv_v + VLEN>=512 + ne1%64==0); arch-fallback aliases
    for all non-riscv arches. Fixed the stock e64 blocker (quantize_mat_
    q8_0_4x8's RVV body now needs __riscv_v, zve32f falls to generic) and
    un-gated quantize_mat_t<1,Q8_0> from zvfh (generic 4x1 otherwise).
    NEW TEST tests/test-repack-q1_0.cpp (extra-buft mul_mat vs default-buft
    reference; test-backend-ops skips CPU-only so it cannot see repack):
    RED = zero-stub 3/3 FAIL nmse=1.0; GREEN = 3/3 OK nmse=0 (bit-exact) at
    QEMU VLEN=512 AND 1024 (rv64gcv build); x86 host = clean SKIP.
    Build note: repack path needs march WITH v/zve32f - build-rv64 now
    configured -march=rv64gcv -mext-zvlsseg (ELEN=64 decision, premium_max).
    K=51 MEASURED on fpga_l3 (2026-07-24, andesim hybrid marker, Bonsai-4B,
    same cmdline as baseline): 4,476,168 -> 2,144,755 cycles = 2.09x on the
    whole MUL_MAT node. Gap vs lab 6.6x is expected: in-model the 2560x1024
    weights (360KB repacked) stream from L3 (L1 32K only),
    activation quantize is scalar generic (no zvfh build), plus node
    overheads; the lab strip was L1-resident.
    WEIGHTS-IN-HVM DONE (2026-07-25, same K=51 ROI; committed q1_0-rvv-opt
    510479ad8): ggml-cpu/hvm.h + repack set_tensor redirect, gated by env
    GGML_Q1_HVM or -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v (off by default). At load the
    selected Q1_0 repack tensors are written straight into HVM (0x90000000;
    fpga_l3's 8MB window holds 22 attn_v weights, the bump allocator overflows
    the rest back to RAM), so the per-column sign-plane stream reads banked
    local memory, not L3. K=51 blk.7.attn_v is in HVM ([roi] print confirms
    src0). HEADLINE: baseline (pristine vec_dot, weights in L3/cache)
    4,476,168 -> optimized (repack row-parallel kernel + weights in HVM)
    946,460 = 4.73x end-to-end. Breakdown: repack kernel alone (both in RAM)
    2.09x, then HVM alone (same kernel, RAM->HVM) a further 2.27x.
    CORRECTNESS VERIFIED bit-exact: HVM-on vs no-HVM
    binaries (both VLEN 1024, greedy) produce byte-identical output
    ("...Paris. Paris is the capital of France...") -- the win is on a correct
    kernel, not a broken one. Verified through a new andesim capability: fast
    mode now accepts a vsim engine and -readconfig's its HVM geometry, so the
    whole model runs functionally under HVM with no cycle leg (andesim
    feat(run) 5f039b5). Remaining levers: activation quantize RVV (e32-clean),
    M>1 prefill tiles, F6 ACE.
    ROI-counter fix included: MUL_MAT counting moved BEFORE the extra-buffer
    dispatch in ggml_compute_forward (repacked matmuls return early there;
    counting in the switch case would skip them and shift K).
    premium_max K=51 BLOCKED on vsim_andesim: ax45 subsystem hybrid resume
    cannot halt the hart - DM debug-entry fetches to 0xE6800000 (PLDM
    region) leave the cluster unserved ("target socket not found", then
    ResumeDriver halt timeout; --no-reset-baseline moves the failure from
    capture to resume). ax46 serves this internally (hybrid was developed
    there); both RTLs contain u_pldm, same debug cfg - the gap is ax45
    wrapper/platform wiring in vsim_andesim, NOT the engine cfg (QEMU leg
    exits 200, standalone ELF runs fine). Premium in-model number waits on
    that fix; lab numbers (canonical table) stand in the meantime.
- Gate: K=51 ROI (V projection 2560x1024 gemv is exactly the accelerated
  shape) on both engines; graph node count is unchanged by repack, so K=51
  stays valid.
- Relationship to F6 (xandesvdot): F4b is Strategy A (base RVV, no
  dot-product). F6 is Strategy B on the SAME repack layout - expand signs to
  +-1 int8 once, let NDS.VD4DOTS do the K-reduction in-lane. They compose;
  decision gate is a cycle-accurate A-vs-B shootout (marker ROI or ace-tq1).
- Key files:
  - kernel-lab/ (F4a/F4b reference + test first)
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp (repack fn + traits dispatch, ~line 3200 /
    3868 templates; 16x1 gemv reference at :1370)
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp (RVV microkernels; 8x8 at :114)
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.h (block<Q,N> types, gemv/gemm decls)
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch-fallback.h:206+ (remove new symbols from fallback)
- Dependencies: F4a is independent and is the best first step overall.

## F5. Q2_0 (ternary) RISC-V RVV kernel - currently pure scalar

- Status: TODO
- Description: Ternary-Bonsai models use GGML_TYPE_Q2_0 (ggml.h:432). On
  RISC-V it falls back to generic C (arch-fallback.h:209 aliases
  ggml_vec_dot_q2_0_q8_0 to the scalar version in
  ggml/src/ggml-cpu/quants.c:177). x86/ARM have optimized versions; RISC-V
  has none - a ready-made gap. Structure mirrors the Q1_0 kernel: 2-bit
  {-1,0,+1} weights can be handled with two masks + vmerge, or vrgather
  lookup. Reference the TQ2_0 RVV kernel (riscv/quants.c:6300) for a
  similar shape.
- Model: Ternary-Bonsai-4B-Q2_0.gguf (download pending).
- Key files:

## F6. Q1_0 ACE-RVV custom instruction co-design (COPILOT)

- Status: TODO - design fixed 2026-07-20; user confirmed int8 dot-product
  HW exists and wants to design custom ACE-RVV instructions (not just use
  stock xandesvdot). Awaiting user pick of candidate A/B/C before csim work.
- Toolchain / template: user's ACE lab at
  /local/nick/vsim-workspace/vsim-demo/ace-tq1 (COPILOT 7.3, AX46MPV,
  vlen=256 sim). unpack.ace already defines: `v_w_mul_free_macc`
  (multiply-free widening MAC, weight in {-1,0,1}: result_2int += act_i8 (*)
  weight_i8, no multiplier) and trit `unpack` insns. tq1.c dataflow =
  unpack -> v_w_mul_free_macc -> ONE vwredsum/256-block -> one scale (works
  because TQ1 pairs with Q8_K = 1 scale/256). Q1_0 pairs with 4x Q8_0 =
  1 scale/32; that mismatch is what the ACE insn must erase.
- Operand model (from unpack.ace): `rvv_insn N { operand = {io|in|out
  vrf:{int|2int|4int|uint} ...}; vector_unit = elen; csim = %{..%};
  latency = 1; }`. vrf:int=i8 lane, 2int/4int=widened i16/i32 result,
  uint=packed bytes. v_q_tq2_unpack already returns 4int (i32) from a packed
  byte -> in-lane widening + reading a packed bit-plane is in-idiom.
- Candidates (precise I/O):
  * A. `v_q1_rowdot` - ROW-PARALLEL K-way sign-dot, THE wide-VLEN optimum.
    Pairs with F4 Nx1 repack: lanes = rows, activation broadcast (splat like
    the q4_0_8x8 vmv_v_x_i64 trick), each lane holds one row's sign bits;
    in-lane 4-way sign-dot, accumulate per row. NO reduction, full VLEN.
      rvv_insn v_q1_rowdot {   // result[lane] += sum_{i<4}(bit_i? +act_i : -act_i)
        operand = { io vrf:4int result, in vrf:int activation, in vrf:uint signbits };
        vector_unit = elen; latency = 1; }
    Sign-bit analog of NDS.VD4DOTS but weight stays 1-bit (8x less reg
    traffic) and the multiplier is just a conditional-negate add-tree
    (cheaper HW than v_w_mul_free_macc). RECOMMENDED.
  * C. `v_q1_sign_macc` - fused single-row (stays in vec_dot shape). Element-
    wise; still needs the per-32 vwredsum tail.
      rvv_insn v_q1_sign_macc {   // result[j] += (bit_j? +act[j] : -act[j])
        operand = { io vrf:2int result, in vrf:int activation, in vrf:uint signbits };
        vector_unit = elen; latency = 1; }
  * B. `v_q1_unpack` - minimal: bits -> +-1 int8 (mirror v_q_tq2_unpack),
    then reuse existing v_w_mul_free_macc + vwredsum. Smallest new HW.
- Decision (defaults if user stays away): pick A. Even the TQ1 one-reduce-
  per-block under-fills a wide register (128/1024 lanes at VLEN=2048); only
  row-parallel turns those lanes into output rows and removes the reduction.
  A shares F4's exact Nx1 layout, so base-RVV (F4b) and ACE (this) run on
  the same repacked weights -> direct vsim A/B shootout.
- Activation format: keep per-32 Q8_0 for path A (row-parallel applies the 4
  per-32 scales as 4 vector FMAs, still zero reduction, no accuracy loss).
  Only paths B/C benefit from coarsening to 1 scale/128 (Q8_K-style, matches
  Q1_0's block) to get a single reduce like TQ1 - costs a bit of activation
  precision, needs a perplexity check.

## F7. zicbop prefetch of next block - DONE 2026-07-27 (no HVM)

- Status: DONE. Pure-software win, no HVM. This is the path taken after the
  user dropped HVM (HVM maxes at 256 MiB address space and could hold only
  ~1.4% of the 560 MB Q1_0 weights at the fpga_l3 8 MiB size, so it does not
  generalize; software prefetch helps EVERY Q1_0 matmul).
- Why it works: the row-parallel gemv streams `block_q1_0x64` sequentially
  (`bx[l]`, 2176 B = 34 cache lines each). This core's HW prefetcher is shallow
  (`NDS_L3C_PFP_LINE_NUM=0`, D$ 4 entries), so it cannot run far enough ahead
  to hide the L3/DRAM miss latency that makes the repacked kernel load-bound.
  A `__builtin_prefetch` of the block `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST` ahead pulls it in
  early.
- CORRECTION to the old note: the march did NOT already include zicbop - it is
  behind the `GGML_RV_ZICBOP` CMake option (off by default), and without it
  `__builtin_prefetch` compiles to a nop. Build must pass `-DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON`
  (added to build.sh; gcc 14.2 then emits real `prefetch.r`).
- Measured (K=51 ROI, fpga_l3 VLEN 1024, cycle-accurate vsim). Prefetch
  distance sweep (ALL rows already use repack; DIST=0 = prefetch off):
    DIST=0 (baseline repack)  2,144,213
    DIST=1                    1,391,650   1.54x   <- BEST, shipped default
    DIST=2                    1,430,534   1.50x
    DIST=4                    1,506,429   1.42x
  More lookahead is worse - one 34-line block ahead already covers the latency;
  further only adds MSHR/cache pressure.
- Stacked vs the ORIGINAL kernel (no repack, upstream per-row vec_dot with the
  per-32 vwredsum reduction):
    original (no repack)            4,476,168   1.00x
    repack (F4)                     2,144,213   2.09x
    repack + prefetch DIST=1 (F7)   1,391,650   3.22x
  The two wins are independent and stack: repack fixes the compute (no idle
  lanes at wide VLEN), prefetch fixes the memory (weight stream no longer
  stalls on L3/DRAM misses).
- Correctness: bit-identical text vs baseline (andesim --mode fast, greedy),
  and `prefetch.r` is architecturally a no-op hint (no reg/mem write, no fault).
- Key files:
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp: helper `q1_prefetch_block` +
    one call at the top of each gemv l-loop; `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST` macro
    (default 1, override at build time).
  - build.sh: `-DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON`.
- GEMM (prefill) path prefetched too (same helper in both `q1_gemm_64x1_*`
  l-loops), but the win is marginal: on a PURE-gemm node (nrows=4, one M-tile,
  no gemv remainder) 1,696,704 -> 1,649,275 = **1.03x**. Reason: gemm loads
  each weight block once and reuses it across the M-tile of 4 activations, so
  it is ~4x less memory-bound than gemv (which streams the weight per single
  column) - there is little miss latency left to hide. Kept anyway: correct,
  ~free, small prefill gain. Prefetch's real value is gemv/decode (1.54x).
- MEASUREMENT GOTCHA (found here): the ROI at K=51 was landing in llama.cpp's
  WARMUP forward pass (nrows=2 -> pure gemv, gemm never runs). Use `--no-warmup`
  so #51 becomes the real prefill layer-7 V-proj with nrows = prompt tokens.
  The `[roi]` print now also shows `nrows` (ggml-cpu.c). Prompt token count
  sets the node type: "The capital of France" = 4 tok = pure gemm; "...is" =
  5 tok = gemm(4)+gemv(1); warmup = 2 = pure gemv.

---
name: andes-toolchain-rvv-segment-flag
description: Andes RISC-V GCC gates RVV segment load/store intrinsics behind -mext-zvlsseg; check vendor -m flags before patching source
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f8083144-88fa-478d-bc3e-92321463e7b4
---

The Andes toolchain (`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc`, GCC 14.2, target `riscv64-linux`) does NOT enable RVV tuple segment load/store intrinsics (`__riscv_vlseg*`, `__riscv_vsseg*`, tuple `vcreate`/`vget`) with plain `-march=rv64gcv`. They are gated behind Andes-specific machine flags:

- `-mext-zvlsseg` - segment load/store
- `-mext-zvlss` - strided load/store
- `-mext-zvlsidx` - indexed load/store

**Why:** Andes vector units make these instruction groups optional, so the fork hides the intrinsics unless the flag is given. Errors look like "implicit declaration of __riscv_vlseg2e32_v_u32mf2x2", which wrongly suggests the intrinsics are missing.

**How to apply:** When an intrinsic is "not declared" under this toolchain, first check `riscv64-linux-gcc --target-help | grep -i <feature>` for a `-mext-*` flag. Do not rewrite the source. For llama.cpp rv64 builds, pass `-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg`. Working cross-build configure (build dir `build-rv64`):

```
cmake -B build-rv64 \
  -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=$TC/riscv64-linux-gcc -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$TC/riscv64-linux-g++ \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg \
  -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF
```

ggml then compiles the CPU backend with `-march=rv64gcv_zfh_zvfh_zicbop_zihintpause -mabi=lp64d` (GGML_RVV/GGML_RV_ZFH/GGML_RV_ZVFH/GGML_RV_ZICBOP default ON).

**Running the result under QEMU (user-mode):** stock `/usr/bin/qemu-riscv64` SIGILLs in ld.so (sysroot glibc uses xandes custom opcodes). Use the Andes linux-user QEMU at `/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-qemu/linux/qemu-riscv64` (also `build-qemu-ast542/linux/`). Critical: `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` does NOT enable zvfh by default, so ggml's `vfncvt.f.f.w` in `ggml_cpu_fp32_to_fp16` SIGILLs - add `zfh=true,zvfh=true`. Working command:

```
/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-qemu/linux/qemu-riscv64 \
  -L $TOOLCHAIN_ROOT/sysroot \
  -E LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<build>/bin \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512,zfh=true,zvfh=true \
  <build>/bin/llama-bench -m <model.gguf> ...

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the RISC-V llama-completion binaries for the Q1_0 prefetch reproduce
# runbook (q1_0_hvm_reproduce.md): pristine / baseline / prefetch (+ optional hvm).
#   pristine = upstream kernel, no repack
#   baseline = repack row-parallel kernel, prefetch OFF (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0)
#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   hvm      = repack + weights-in-HVM (older experiment, now superseded)
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh prefetch           # just the shipped kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# Which MUL_MAT node the ROI brackets. Compile-time because andesim's linux
# runtime hands the guest an EMPTY envp (runtime/linux/stack.h), so the
# GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_K env override never reaches the guest -- one binary per
# measured node. Bonsai-4B layer 7 (see q1_0_hvm_reproduce.md shape table):
#   50 attn_q  51 attn_v  52 attn_k  53 attn_output  54 ffn_gate  55 ffn_up
#   56 ffn_down                                       253 result_output
# K=51 keeps the original unsuffixed artifact names; anything else appends -k<K>.
ROI_K=${ROI_K:-51}
SUF=""; [ "$ROI_K" = 51 ] || SUF="-k$ROI_K"

# The settings that MUST be right (else the guest crashes / baseline is wrong):
#   -static                : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK      : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON    : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                            gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)
#   -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=N   : prefetch lookahead in blocks; 0 = off (baseline), 1 = shipped
#   -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME     : HVM redirect selector; only on the HVM build
cfg() {  # $1 build dir   $2 repack toggle   $3 extra defines (DIST / HVM selector, or "")
  local FL="$3 -mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM/build/runtime/include"
  cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$1" \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF \
    -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
    -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON \
    -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
    $2 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
  cmake --build "$1" --target llama-completion -j"$(nproc)"
}

build_one() {  # $1 = pristine | baseline | prefetch | hvm
  case "$1" in
    pristine) cfg "$LLAMA/b-pristine$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF" "" ;;
    baseline) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    prefetch) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    hvm)      cfg "$LLAMA/b-hvm$SUF"      "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v" ;;
    # A/B pair for "does prefetch.r depend on the D$ prefetch unit": same
    # kernels, but the ROI runs with mcache_ctl.DPREF_EN cleared.
    prefetch-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    baseline-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    *) echo "unknown target '$1' (want pristine|baseline|prefetch|hvm|*-nodpref)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  cp "$LLAMA/b-$1$SUF/bin/llama-completion" "$LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF"
  echo "built: $LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF (ROI MUL_MAT #$ROI_K)"
}

for t in ${*:-pristine baseline prefetch}; do build_one "$t"; done

content.text:
Yes - `opt_roadmap.md` F6 (lines 284-348) is the ACE-RVV item, still TODO. But while checking it I found something that changes the answer: **your target RTL already has Andes vendor dot-product instructions, so you may not need custom ACE at all.**

## 1. What F6 in the roadmap says

Three candidates, A recommended:

| | insn | shape | new HW |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `v_q1_rowdot` | 4-way sign-dot, lanes = rows, no reduction, pairs with the F4 Nx1 repack | most |
| B | `v_q1_unpack` | bits -> +-1 int8, then reuse `v_w_mul_free_macc` | least |
| C | `v_q1_sign_macc` | single-row, still needs the per-32 `vwredsum` tail | mid |

It was written before F4/F7 landed, and it assumed you must build the instruction yourself with COPILOT.

## 2. New facts (checked just now, not from memory)

- `/local/nick/vsim/data/configs/ax46mpv_fpga_l3.cfg` ISA string already contains `xandesvdot1p0 xandesvqmac1p0 xandessintload1p0 xandesvpackfph1p0`. `NDS_VECTOR_VDOT_SUPPORT = yes` on **all three** engines (premium, premium_full, fpga_l3).
- The Andes GCC 14.2 assembler knows these already: `nds.vd4dots.vv` (+ `.vv u`/`su`), `nds.vqmacc.*`, `nds.vln8.v` (load nibbles -> int8), `nds.vle4.v`, `nds.vfwcvt.f.b.v` (byte -> float, one op), `nds.vfpmadb/t.vf` (packed fp16 MAC). I compiled and disassembled one: `1388445b nds.vd4dots.vv v8,v16,v24`.
- **No intrinsics** in GCC 14.2 (`__riscv_nds_vd4dots_*` = implicit declaration). Inline asm only.
- Not verified: whether QEMU executes `nds.vd4dots` (you stopped me mid-test), and the exact operand semantics. Both need one small run before committing.

So F6 splits into: **B-stock** (use `nds.vd4dots`, zero new hardware, works today) vs **A-custom** (COPILOT + RTL, 1-bit weight native).

## 3. How much is actually left to win

From your own measured points on K=51 / fpga_l3:

| build | cycles | |
|---|---|---|
| pristine | 4,476,168 | 1.00x |
| repack (F4) | 2,144,213 | 2.09x |
| repack + prefetch (F7) | 1,391,650 | 3.22x |
| repack + HVM (weights in local RAM) | 946,460 | 4.73x |

The HVM number is the same kernel with memory stalls removed, so it is close to a pure-compute floor. Today's 1.39M is roughly **68% compute, 32% memory**. ACE / vdot only attacks the compute part:
- absolute ceiling if compute became free: ~0.45M (3.1x more)
- realistic (3-4x fewer hot-loop ops): ~0.6-0.75M, so **about 1.8-2.3x**

## 4. What vdot changes in the kernel

Now, per column per 64-row tile (`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1789-1794`): `vlm` + `vsub.vx` + masked `vadd.vx` = 3 vector ops, and the two ALU ops form a **serial loop-carried chain** on `sumi`.

With `nds.vd4dots`, per **4 columns**: `vlm` + `vmerge` (bits -> +-1 int8) + activation splat + `vd4dots` = 4 ops.
- ~3x fewer vector ops
- chain becomes 1 op per 4 columns instead of 8 -> **8x shorter dependency chain**
- accumulator is i32, so `vsext.vf2` disappears
- cost: the repacked sign bits must be reordered (4 columns per row byte-lane instead of column-major planes). That is a load-time change, free at run time.

## 5. Cheaper first (pure RVV, no new HW, same bottleneck)

11.5 cycles per column-tile even in HVM, for 3 instructions, says you are **latency-chain bound, not throughput bound**. Two software fixes attack exactly that:

1. **bsums trick** (same one in your ace-tq1 notes): drop the per-column `vsub`. Sum the 32 activation values once as a scalar, do only the masked `vadd` per column, subtract `sum_y` once per group. 3 ops -> 2 ops per column, chain 2 -> 1. No overflow risk (max 8128 in int16).
2. **Split accumulators**: 2-4 independent `sumi` registers over interleaved columns, add them at group end. Breaks the loop-carried chain. Registers are free at i16m1/VLEN=1024.

Both are hours of work in `kernel-lab/` with the existing rdcycle flow. If they land most of the win, the vdot upside shrinks a lot - so measure them first.

## 6. Recommended order

1. bsums + split accumulator (pure RVV, ships everywhere, cheapest)
2. `nds.vd4dots` prototype in kernel-lab, inline asm, A/B on vsim (no RTL work needed)
3. LM head repack gate (rows%64 = 53 fails, ~26% of a decode pass) - bigger than both, and not ACE
4. Custom ACE (real F6-A) only if 2 shows the +-1 form clearly beats int8 vdot

Roadmap is stale on two points: it treats `xandesvdot` as "stock but unexamined", and F6 still says "awaiting user pick of A/B/C". Want me to update F6 with these findings?

-include ../Make.var

CC:=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gcc
OBJDUMP:=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)objdump

# Toolchain DEFAULT runtime + -mvh (Andes virtual hosting): no custom
# crt0/libgloss/handler. The same ELF runs on Andes QEMU and on vsim.
# No zfh/zvfh in march: premium has neither; fp16 scales are expanded with
# integer vector ops (fp32 math needs zve32f).
CFLAGS:= -march=rv$(XLEN)gc_zve32f -mvh -O2 -ffp-contract=off -fno-tree-vectorize

# engines (use the vsim_andesim builds - RAM to 0x8fffffff, sim_control OK)
# premium_full = premium RTL + FELEN=64 config; the plain premium build has
# NDS_FELEN=0 (no vector FP - every vf* traps), do not use it for this kernel
SIM_PREMIUM ?= /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium_full
SIM_FPGA_L3 ?= /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3
# premium RTL reparameterized to ELEN=64/FELEN=64/packed-FP16/32K D$
SIM_PREMIUM_MAX ?= /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium_max

# vsim flavor: same sources, linked with the vsim BSP (sim_control MMIO I/O);
# vsim does not service -mvh virtual-hosting syscalls, QEMU does not model
# the sim_control device - hence one flavor per runner.
VSIM_LINK := $(VSIM_FILES) $(VSIM_FLAGS) $(VSIM_OPTIMIZE)

all: test_q1_0 test_q1_0_v1024 test_q1_0_vsim test_q1_0_vsim_v1024 test_q1_0.dump

# gemv built for VLEN=512 (i16m2/f32m4) - run on sim_ax45mpv_premium
test_q1_0: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ $(CFLAGS)

# gemv built for VLEN=1024 (i16m1/f32m2) - run on sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3.
# Our objects avoid 'c' (ax46mpv has Zcmp, not Zcd: compressed FP stores are
# illegal there); prelinked libc is rv64gc, so stay on integer-only printf
# (iprintf) to keep libc's float-printf (which has c.fsdsp) out of the link.
test_q1_0_v1024: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ -DQ1_VLEN=1024 $(CFLAGS) -march=rv$(XLEN)g_zve32f

test_q1_0_vsim: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ $(filter-out -mvh,$(CFLAGS)) $(VSIM_LINK)

test_q1_0_vsim_v1024: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ -DQ1_VLEN=1024 $(filter-out -mvh,$(CFLAGS)) -march=rv$(XLEN)g_zve32f $(VSIM_LINK)

# HVM flavors: identical kernels, all data placed in the HVM vector memory
# (hvm.h CSR-probe allocator, ported printf-free from ../ace-tq1/hvm_util.c)
test_q1_0_vsim_hvm: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h hvm.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ -DQ1_HVM=1 $(filter-out -mvh,$(CFLAGS)) $(VSIM_LINK)

test_q1_0_vsim_v1024_hvm: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h hvm.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ -DQ1_HVM=1 -DQ1_VLEN=1024 $(filter-out -mvh,$(CFLAGS)) -march=rv$(XLEN)g_zve32f $(VSIM_LINK)

test_q1_0.dump: test_q1_0
	$(OBJDUMP) $< -d > $@

run: test_q1_0_vsim
	$(SIM_PREMIUM) $<

run-1024: test_q1_0_vsim_v1024
	$(SIM_FPGA_L3) $<

# probe with full-V march so the e64/f64/fp16 acceptance cases compile
probe_max: probe.c
	$(CC) $< -o $@ -march=rv$(XLEN)gcv $(filter-out -march=%,$(filter-out -mvh,$(CFLAGS))) $(VSIM_LINK)

run-probe-max: probe_max
	$(SIM_PREMIUM_MAX) $<

run-hvm: test_q1_0_vsim_hvm
	$(SIM_PREMIUM) $<

run-1024-hvm: test_q1_0_vsim_v1024_hvm
	$(SIM_FPGA_L3) $<

clean:
	- rm -f test_q1_0 test_q1_0_v1024 test_q1_0_vsim* *.o *.dump link.map

.PHONY: clean all run run-1024 run-hvm run-1024-hvm

-include ../Make.var

CC:=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gcc
OBJDUMP:=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)objdump

# Toolchain DEFAULT runtime + -mvh (Andes virtual hosting): no custom
# crt0/libgloss/handler. The same ELF runs on Andes QEMU and on vsim.
# No zfh/zvfh in march: premium has neither; fp16 scales are expanded with
# integer vector ops (fp32 math needs zve32f).
CFLAGS:= -march=rv$(XLEN)gc_zve32f -mvh -O2 -ffp-contract=off -fno-tree-vectorize

# engines (use the vsim_andesim builds - RAM to 0x8fffffff, sim_control OK)
# premium_full = premium RTL + FELEN=64 config; the plain premium build has
# NDS_FELEN=0 (no vector FP - every vf* traps), do not use it for this kernel
SIM_PREMIUM ?= /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium_full
SIM_FPGA_L3 ?= /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3
# premium RTL reparameterized to ELEN=64/FELEN=64/packed-FP16/32K D$
SIM_PREMIUM_MAX ?= /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium_max

# vsim flavor: same sources, linked with the vsim BSP (sim_control MMIO I/O);
# vsim does not service -mvh virtual-hosting syscalls, QEMU does not model
# the sim_control device - hence one flavor per runner.
VSIM_LINK := $(VSIM_FILES) $(VSIM_FLAGS) $(VSIM_OPTIMIZE)

all: test_q1_0 test_q1_0_v1024 test_q1_0_vsim test_q1_0_vsim_v1024 test_q1_0.dump

# gemv built for VLEN=512 (i16m2/f32m4) - run on sim_ax45mpv_premium
test_q1_0: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ $(CFLAGS)

# gemv built for VLEN=1024 (i16m1/f32m2) - run on sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3.
# Our objects avoid 'c' (ax46mpv has Zcmp, not Zcd: compressed FP stores are
# illegal there); prelinked libc is rv64gc, so stay on integer-only printf
# (iprintf) to keep libc's float-printf (which has c.fsdsp) out of the link.
test_q1_0_v1024: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ -DQ1_VLEN=1024 $(CFLAGS) -march=rv$(XLEN)g_zve32f

test_q1_0_vsim: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ $(filter-out -mvh,$(CFLAGS)) $(VSIM_LINK)

test_q1_0_vsim_v1024: main.c q1_0.c q1_0.h
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ -DQ1_VLEN=1024 $(filter-out -mvh,$(CFLAGS)) -march=rv$(XLEN)g_zve32f $(VSIM_LINK)

# HVM flavors: identical kernels, all data placed in the HVM vector memory
# (hvm.h CSR-probe allocator, ported printf-free from ../ace-tq1/hvm_util.c)

p='q1_0_d4.c'
s=open(p).read()

extra = r'''
// ---- isolation legs: which of the four shared ops costs the cycles? --------
// v2 and v1 differ 3.4x in instruction count but run at the same speed, so the
// cost sits in what they share per 4 columns: vlm, vmerge, the activation
// broadcast, and the dot itself. v3 swaps the strided broadcast for lw+vmv.v.x;
// nodot additionally replaces the dot with a plain vadd (WRONG results, timing
// only). v2-v3 = broadcast cost, v3-nodot = nds.vd4dots cost.
#define D4_TILE16_BC(DOT0, DOT1, DOT2, DOT3, acc0, acc1, planes, acts)     \
    asm volatile(                                                          \
        "vsetvli t0, zero, e8, m2, ta, ma\n\t"                             \
        "mv      t1, %2\n\t"                                               \
        "vmv.v.i v2, -1\n\t"                                               \
        "vlm.v   v0, (t1)\n\t"                                             \
        "vmerge.vim v4, v2, 1, v0\n\t"                                     \
        "addi    t1, t1, 32\n\t"                                           \
        "vlm.v   v0, (t1)\n\t"                                             \
        "vmerge.vim v6, v2, 1, v0\n\t"                                     \
        "addi    t1, t1, 32\n\t"                                           \
        "vlm.v   v0, (t1)\n\t"                                             \
        "vmerge.vim v8, v2, 1, v0\n\t"                                     \
        "addi    t1, t1, 32\n\t"                                           \
        "vlm.v   v0, (t1)\n\t"                                             \
        "vmerge.vim v10, v2, 1, v0\n\t"                                    \
        "vsetvli t0, zero, e32, m2, ta, ma\n\t"                            \
        "lw      t3, 0(%3)\n\t"                                            \
        "vmv.v.x v12, t3\n\t"                                              \
        "lw      t3, 4(%3)\n\t"                                            \
        "vmv.v.x v14, t3\n\t"                                              \
        "lw      t3, 8(%3)\n\t"                                            \
        "vmv.v.x v16, t3\n\t"                                              \
        "lw      t3, 12(%3)\n\t"                                           \
        "vmv.v.x v18, t3\n\t"                                              \
        DOT0 DOT1 DOT2 DOT3                                                \
        : "+vr"(acc0), "+vr"(acc1)                                         \
        : "r"(planes), "r"(acts)                                           \
        : "t0", "t1", "t3",                                                \
          "v0", "v2", "v4", "v6", "v8", "v10", "v12", "v14", "v16", "v18")

#define D4_REAL0 "nds.vd4dots.vv %0, v4,  v12\n\t"
#define D4_REAL1 "nds.vd4dots.vv %1, v6,  v14\n\t"
#define D4_REAL2 "nds.vd4dots.vv %0, v8,  v16\n\t"
#define D4_REAL3 "nds.vd4dots.vv %1, v10, v18"

#define D4_FAKE1 "vadd.vv %1, %1, v6\n\t"
#define D4_FAKE2 "vadd.vv %0, %0, v8\n\t"
#define D4_FAKE3 "vadd.vv %1, %1, v10"

#define D4_BODY(NAME, T0, T1, T2, T3)                                                        \
void NAME(int n, float * s, const block_q1_0_64d4 * bricks, const block_q8_0 * y,            \
          const int8_t * ya, int nr) {                                                       \
    const int nb = n / QK1_0;                                                                \

---
name: xandesvdot-nds-vd4dots-usable
description: XAndesVDot (nds.vd4dots.vv) is already in all 3 vsim engines and the assembler - no COPILOT/ACE needed; how to build/run it, and the vlse32 stride-0 trap that makes it look 18x slower
metadata:
  type: project
---

`nds.vd4dots.vv` (XAndesVDot) is a STOCK Andes vendor instruction, not custom ACE.
Verified 2026-07-29 while answering "what can ace-rvv still optimize" (roadmap F6,
see [[q1_0-wide-vlen-repack-rowparallel]]).

Semantics (verified by running, QEMU + vsim): with vtype `e32`,
`vd[lane] += sum_{k=0..3} vs1[4*lane+k] * vs2[4*lane+k]`, int8 x int8 into the
i32 lane. Source and dest use the SAME LMUL (i8 group reinterpreted as 4 bytes
per 32-bit element).

Availability:
- RTL: `NDS_VECTOR_VDOT_SUPPORT = yes` in ax46mpv_fpga_l3, ax45mpv_premium and
  premium_full cfgs (`/local/nick/vsim/data/configs/*.cfg`). fpga_l3's ISA string
  also carries `xandesvqmac1p0 xandessintload1p0 xandesvpackfph1p0 xandesbfhcvt1p0`
  (nds.vqmacc.*, nds.vln8.v / nds.vle4.v sub-int loads, packed-fp16 MAC,
  nds.vfwcvt.f.b.v byte->float) - all unexplored.
- Assembler: needs `-march=..._xandesvdot1p0` (the VERSION suffix is required on
  older gas; unversioned works only on the ast542 linux toolchain). Baremetal
  toolchains: ast540/541/550 under `/local/ycc738/andes_toolchains/` know the
  mnemonic; **ast533 does NOT** (the q1_0 lab's default - override
  `TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX` on the make command line).
- GCC 14.2 has NO intrinsic (`__riscv_nds_vd4dots_*` = implicit declaration).
  Use inline asm. Safe: GCC treats an asm block as a vtype killer and re-emits
  its own `vsetvli` afterwards, so the asm may set vtype freely.
- QEMU: only `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` executes it. `-cpu andes-ax46mpv` SIGILLs
  (exit 132) even though the helpers are in the binary.

TWO TRAPS on ax46mpv_fpga_l3, both found the hard way:
1. `vlse32.v vd, (rs1), zero` (stride-0 broadcast, which GCC picks for
   `vmv_v_x` from a memory word) is CATASTROPHICALLY slow - element-serial.
   Replacing it with `lw` + `vmv.v.x` took the same kernel from 920 to 50
   cyc/dot (18x). Never let a broadcast become a strided load on this core.
2. The core traps (mcause exception 4, load address misaligned) on a
   misaligned 32-bit VECTOR element load. `block_q8_0` puts `qs` at offset 2,
   so any 4-byte activation group load off `qs` faults - the d4 path needs the
   activation quants in a separate 4-byte-aligned array.

Lab: `/local/nick/vsim-workspace/vsim-demo/q1_0_d4/` (copy of the q1_0 shootout
plus `q1_0_d4.c`; original q1_0/ untouched).

content.text:
`nds.vd4dots` speeds up the Q1_0 gemv by **2.52x**, and needs no ACE/COPILOT work — it is already in the RTL of all three vsim engines.

## Measured (vsim ax46mpv_fpga_l3, VLEN=1024, nr=64 x n=512 x M=4, cyc/dot)

| leg | kernel | cyc/dot | vs [3] |
|---|---|---|---|
| [2] | vl256 per-row (upstream) | 831 | 0.15x |
| [3] | gemv_64x1 (your shipped kernel) | 126 | 1.00x |
| [4] | gemm_64x1, M=4 | 41 | 3.07x |
| [5] | **gemv + nds.vd4dots** | **50** | **2.52x** |
| [6] | control: dot replaced by `vadd` | 52 | - |

Correctness: **ALL PASS**, bit-exact vs the vl256 reference (`qemu-riscv64 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024`). Note the vd4dots gemv (50) is close to your M=4 GEMM (41) — a vd4dots GEMM should go below it.

## What made it work

- **Layout**: sign bits regrouped 4 columns at a time, bit index `4*row + colofs`. Same block size, same repack cost. One `vlm` + one `vmerge` builds the +-1 int8 operand; one dot eats 4 columns.
- **The dot itself is nearly free** — leg [6] proves it: swapping the dot for a plain `vadd` gives 52 vs 50. The 2.52x comes from doing 4 columns per instruction group, which only the dot makes possible.

## Two traps that cost me the most time (both worth remembering)

1. **`vlse32.v (rs1), zero` is catastrophically slow on this core** — element-serial. GCC picks it naturally for a broadcast from memory. Same kernel: **920 cyc/dot with `vlse32`, 50 with `lw` + `vmv.v.x`. 18x.** This is why my first two versions looked like a 7.4x *regression*. Note also that v1 (intrinsics) and v2 (hand-scheduled, 3.4x fewer instructions) ran at identical speed — instruction count was never the bottleneck, one bad instruction was.
2. **The core traps (mcause=4, misaligned load) on a misaligned 32-bit vector element load.** `block_q8_0.qs` sits at offset 2, so activation group loads always fault. The d4 path needs the activation quants in a separate 4-byte-aligned array — free if the activation quantize step writes them that way.

## Build facts

- `-march=..._xandesvdot1p0` (version suffix required on older gas). Toolchains **ast540/541/550** know the mnemonic; **ast533 does not** — that is the q1_0 lab's default, override `TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX`.
- No GCC intrinsic exists; inline asm only. Safe: GCC treats an asm block as a vtype killer and re-emits its own `vsetvli`.
- QEMU runs it on `-cpu andes-ax45mpv`; `andes-ax46mpv` SIGILLs.

## Model-level estimate

K=51 is 1.39M cycles today, ~68% compute (from your HVM data point). 2.5x on the compute part predicts roughly **1.39M -> ~0.82M (~1.7x)**, stacking with prefetch. Not measured in-model yet.

Lab is at `/local/nick/vsim-workspace/vsim-demo/q1_0_d4/` — a copy; your original `q1_0/` is untouched.

Want me to take this into ggml (new block type + aligned activation quants + gated kernel), or first run the in-model K=51 gate?

message.content: 看不懂表格內 3, 4, 5, 6 分別做了什麼

content.text:
各 leg 都算同一件事：64 列 x 512 行的 Q1_0 權重矩陣 乘 4 個 activation 向量 = 4 x 64 = 256 個輸出數字。`cyc/dot` = 總 cycle / 256。數字越小越快。

Difference is only **how** they compute it:

| leg | one call does | calls | inner loop |
|---|---|---|---|
| [2] | 1 row x 1 activation | 256 | old upstream kernel, horizontal reduce per 32 cols |
| [3] | 64 rows x 1 activation | 4 | row-parallel, **3 vector insns per 1 column** |
| [4] | 64 rows x **4** activations | 1 | same as [3], but each mask loaded once and reused 4x |
| [5] | 64 rows x 1 activation | 4 | row-parallel + vd4dots, **4 vector insns per 4 columns** |
| [6] | not a real kernel | 4 | copy of [5] with the dot removed - measurement only |

## [3] vs [5] - the real comparison

Both do the same job with the same call pattern. Only the inner loop differs.

```
[3] per 1 column (64 rows in 64 lanes):
      vlm     v0, mask          64 sign bits, one per row
      vsub.vx sumi, sumi, y     -y in every lane
      vadd.vx sumi, sumi, 2y, v0.t   +2y where bit=1  -> net +-y
    = 3 instructions for 1 column

[5] per 4 columns (64 rows in 64 lanes):
      vlm     v0, mask          4 bits per row = 256 bits
      vmerge  w, -1, +1, v0     turn bits into +-1 int8
      lw + vmv.v.x  a           4 activations, same in every lane
      nds.vd4dots acc, w, a     each lane: acc += 4 products
    = 4 instructions for 4 columns
```

So [5] does 3x less work per column. That is the 126 -> 50.

## Why [4] and [6] are in the table

- **[4] gemm** is not a competitor to [5]. It is a different shape: it needs 4 tokens at the same time, so it only helps **prefill**, not decode. I listed it to show the scale - [5] at 50 almost reaches [4] at 41, using only 1 activation.
- **[6] nodot** answers "is the new instruction itself fast or slow?". It is [5] with `nds.vd4dots` replaced by a plain `vadd.vv`. The answer is wrong on purpose - it only measures the cost of everything else. Result 52 vs [5] 50: the dot costs nothing extra. So the win comes from the loop shape (4 columns per group), and the dot is what makes that shape possible.

---
name: xandesvdot-nds-vd4dots-usable
description: "XAndesVDot (nds.vd4dots.vv) is already in all 3 vsim engines and the assembler - no COPILOT/ACE needed; how to build/run it, and the vlse32 stride-0 trap that makes it look 18x slower"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ebfb04e0-19ef-4a1a-9e2c-58953c138710
  modified: 2026-07-29T01:22:32.004Z
---

`nds.vd4dots.vv` (XAndesVDot) is a STOCK Andes vendor instruction, not custom ACE.
Verified 2026-07-29 while answering "what can ace-rvv still optimize" (roadmap F6,
see [[q1_0-wide-vlen-repack-rowparallel]]).

Semantics (verified by running, QEMU + vsim): with vtype `e32`,
`vd[lane] += sum_{k=0..3} vs1[4*lane+k] * vs2[4*lane+k]`, int8 x int8 into the
i32 lane. Source and dest use the SAME LMUL (i8 group reinterpreted as 4 bytes
per 32-bit element).

Availability:
- RTL: `NDS_VECTOR_VDOT_SUPPORT = yes` in ax46mpv_fpga_l3, ax45mpv_premium and
  premium_full cfgs (`/local/nick/vsim/data/configs/*.cfg`). fpga_l3's ISA string
  also carries `xandesvqmac1p0 xandessintload1p0 xandesvpackfph1p0 xandesbfhcvt1p0`
  (nds.vqmacc.*, nds.vln8.v / nds.vle4.v sub-int loads, packed-fp16 MAC,
  nds.vfwcvt.f.b.v byte->float) - all unexplored.
- Assembler: needs `-march=..._xandesvdot1p0` (the VERSION suffix is required on
  older gas; unversioned works only on the ast542 linux toolchain). Baremetal
  toolchains: ast540/541/550 under `/local/ycc738/andes_toolchains/` know the
  mnemonic; **ast533 does NOT** (the q1_0 lab's default - override
  `TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX` on the make command line).
- GCC 14.2 has NO intrinsic (`__riscv_nds_vd4dots_*` = implicit declaration).
  Use inline asm. Safe: GCC treats an asm block as a vtype killer and re-emits
  its own `vsetvli` afterwards, so the asm may set vtype freely.
- QEMU: only `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` executes it. `-cpu andes-ax46mpv` SIGILLs
  (exit 132) even though the helpers are in the binary.

TWO TRAPS on ax46mpv_fpga_l3, both found the hard way:
1. `vlse32.v vd, (rs1), zero` (stride-0 broadcast, which GCC picks for
   `vmv_v_x` from a memory word) is CATASTROPHICALLY slow - element-serial.
   Replacing it with `lw` + `vmv.v.x` took the same kernel from 920 to 50
   cyc/dot (18x). Never let a broadcast become a strided load on this core.
2. The core traps (mcause exception 4, load address misaligned) on a
   misaligned 32-bit VECTOR element load. `block_q8_0` puts `qs` at offset 2,
   so any 4-byte activation group load off `qs` faults - the d4 path needs the
   activation quants in a separate 4-byte-aligned array.

RESULT (vsim ax46mpv_fpga_l3, VLEN=1024, nr=64 x n=512 x M=4, cyc/dot):
  [2] vl256 per-row original 831 | [3] gemv_64x1 (shipped) 126 |
  [4] gemm_64x1 M=4 41 | [5] gemv + nds.vd4dots **50** = 2.52x over [3].
Bit-exact vs the vl256 reference (ALL PASS, qemu-riscv64 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024).
The dot itself is ~free: swapping it for a plain vadd gives 52 vs 50 - the win is
processing 4 columns per instruction group, which only the dot makes possible.
Layout needed: sign bits regrouped per 4 columns, bit index = 4*row + colofs
(same block size as block_q1_0x64).

Lab: `/local/nick/vsim-workspace/vsim-demo/q1_0_d4/` (copy of the q1_0 shootout
plus `q1_0_d4.c`; original q1_0/ untouched).

# Hybrid K=51 ROI cycle measurement for the prefetch reproduce runbook
# (q1_0_hvm_reproduce.md). Prints, per binary, the [roi] self-check line
# (now including nrows) and the [andesim] <N> cycles figure for the K=51 node.
#
#   bash measure.sh                     # pristine baseline prefetch (gemv/decode node)
#   bash measure.sh baseline prefetch   # just the prefetch A/B
#   PROMPT="The capital of France" WARMUP=--no-warmup bash measure.sh baseline prefetch
#                                       # pure-gemm node (nrows=4): measures the gemm path
#
# GEMV (decode) node = the warmup forward pass, nrows=2. Expected K=51 cycles:
#   pristine 4,476,168 -> baseline 2,144,213 -> prefetch 1,391,650
#   (prefetch = 1.54x vs baseline, 3.22x vs pristine)
# GEMM (prefill) node = --no-warmup + a 4-token prompt, nrows=4 (pure gemm):
#   baseline 1,696,704 -> prefetch 1,649,275 (only 1.03x - gemm reuses each
#   weight block across the M-tile of 4, so it is ~compute-bound, little to hide)
#
#
# Other shapes: the measured node is compile-time (see build.sh ROI_K), so a
# shape sweep passes the suffixed binaries, e.g.
#   bash measure.sh pristine-k54 baseline-k54 prefetch-k54   # blk.7.ffn_gate
# Bonsai-4B has 6 distinct Q1_0 shapes; layer 7 covers all of them at
# ROI_K = 50 attn_q / 51 attn_v / 52 attn_k / 53 attn_output / 54 ffn_gate /
# 55 ffn_up / 56 ffn_down. Cost scales with rows*K, so ffn_* is ~9.5x the
# attn_v node -> raise TIMEOUT for those.
#
# Slow: the RTL leg runs at a few kHz -> minutes per binary. Override via env
# LLAMA / ANDESIM / MODEL / ENGINE / PROMPT / WARMUP / TIMEOUT.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
MODEL=${MODEL:-$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}
ENGINE=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3}
PROMPT=${PROMPT:-The capital of France is}
WARMUP=${WARMUP:-}
TIMEOUT=${TIMEOUT:-14400000}   # hybrid per-leg spawn timeout, ms (4h)

for b in ${*:-pristine baseline prefetch}; do
  echo "=== $b ==="
  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
      --mem-size 2000M --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms "$TIMEOUT" \
      "$LLAMA/bin-$b" -- -m "$MODEL" -no-cnv $WARMUP --prompt "$PROMPT" \
      -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 ) 2>&1 | grep -E '\[roi\]|\[andesim\] .*cycles'
done
